name: Shakti Peethas of the South
theme: The six southern seats of the Goddess among the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas praised in the hymn ascribed to Adi Shankara
region: Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
description: The Shakti Peethas are seats of the Goddess that, in the widely told legend, arose where parts of the body of Sati fell as Shiva carried her through the worlds after Daksha's sacrifice. A hymn ascribed to Adi Shankara names eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas across the subcontinent, and six of them lie in the South: Kamakshi at Kanchipuram, Chamundeshwari on Chamundi Hill above Mysuru, Jogulamba at Alampur on the Tungabhadra, Bhramaramba at Srisailam beside the Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga, Puruhutika at Pithapuram and Manikyamba at Draksharamam. This circuit follows the order in which the hymn lists them, from the Tamil country north through the Deccan to the Godavari delta, and is a natural pilgrimage during Navaratri.
